newsitem.title: LATVIA: KRASTS GOVERNMENT GETS PARLIAMENT SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: KRASTS GOVERNMENT GETS PARLIAMENT SUPPORT.

text.p: Latvia's parliament on Thursday confirmed the government of Prime Minister Guntar Krasts in office by an overwhelming majority.
A vote in support of the government had been expected as the coalition is formed from six parties that command 67 seats in the 100-seat parliament.
The vote backed the government with 73 votes, 13 members of parliament voted against and three MPs abstained, the parliament press office said.
Krasts has pledged to pursue economic reforms and try and prepare Latvia to begin talks for European Union (EU) entry in a first wave of expansion.
He has also said he wants to follow the tough fiscal and budgetary policy of his predecessor Andris Shkele.
The policies include a balanced budget but there have been doubts that the different parties in the coalition will be able to pull together and cap spending sufficiently.
Finance Minister Robert Zile has said he would resign if the government drops the idea of a balanced budget.
